failNotConstructibleReason: As of this catalogs.db snapshot, 0 rows in cfdi_40_productos_servicios and 0 rows in cfdi_40_claves_unidades have vigencia_hasta populated (confirmed by direct query 2026-08-05) -- there is no real ClaveProdServ/ClaveUnidad whose vigency has actually lapsed to build a naturally-occurring fail case from, and registry.json's own notes for this rule explicitly warn against fabricating a fake catalog row to force one. Existence-only invalidity (a ClaveProdServ/ClaveUnidad that never existed) is already caught by XSD validation (Phase 1, both catalogs are xs:enumeration-typed) before this rule would ever run, so that path can't produce a fail fixture for this rule either without duplicating the XSD test. Revisit if a future catalogs.db refresh adds a real expired row.

notes: This rule has 6 independent sub-cases gated by TipoDeComprobante (CondicionesDePago; Concepto/@Descuento; Comprobante/@Descuento; Impuestos node; FormaPago; MetodoPago), same 'one strongest branch' pattern as moneda-tipocambio-consistencia. pass.xml is a TipoDeComprobante='P' comprobante (Recepcion de pagos) with all 6 forbidden fields correctly absent and SubTotal/Total correctly at 0. fail.xml is identical except it illegally adds Comprobante/@FormaPago='01' and Comprobante/@MetodoPago='PUE' -- sub-cases 5 and 6 of the spec's condition, both gated on TipoDeComprobante in {'T','N','P'} / {'T','P'} respectively, both backed by 2+ independently-confirmed sources (CFDI40103 for FormaPago, CFDI40125 for MetodoPago) per registry.json's satReference, the strongest-cited of the rule's 6 sub-cases. Because both sub-cases are gated to fire simultaneously for this fixture's TipoDeComprobante='P', the rule's own condition text ('un mismo comprobante puede disparar varios a la vez... no colapsarlos') means fail.xml correctly produces TWO Findings for this ruleId, not one -- expectedFailFindingCount reflects that deliberately, see rules.test.ts. NOT covered by a fixture: sub-case 1 (CondicionesDePago, no CFDI40 code found despite active search), sub-case 2 (Concepto/@Descuento, CFDI40111), sub-case 3 (Comprobante/@Descuento, no dedicated CFDI40 code beyond the CFDI40111 cross-reference), and sub-case 4 (Impuestos node, CFDI40201 confirmed only for T/P branch, not the N branch).

This rule has 3 independent sub-cases (Traslado/@Base rollup, CFDI40215; Traslado/@Importe rollup, CFDI40221; Retencion/@Importe rollup, CFDI40211), same 'one strongest branch' pattern as moneda-tipocambio-consistencia. Both fixtures use a two-Concepto comprobante where each Concepto carries its own IVA-16% Traslado (Base 3000.00/Importe 480.00 and Base 2000.00/Importe 320.00, summing to Base 5000.00/Importe 800.00). pass.xml's Comprobante/Impuestos/Traslados/Traslado matches that rollup exactly (Base=5000.00, Importe=800.00). fail.xml changes only Comprobante/Impuestos/Traslados/Traslado/@Importe (and TotalImpuestosTrasladados and Total to match it internally) from 800.00 to 850.00, which no longer equals the sum of the two Concepto-level Traslado/@Importe entries (CFDI40221) -- Base is left correct (still 5000.00, matching the Concepto-level sum) so this exercises only the Importe-rollup sub-case, not the Base-rollup sub-case. TotalImpuestosTrasladados is kept internally consistent with the (wrong) Comprobante-level Traslado/@Importe so impuestos-totales-consistencia (the shallower Resumen-vs-renglon check) does not also fire, and Total is kept consistent with SubTotal+TotalImpuestosTrasladados so total-comprobante-consistencia does not also fire -- isolating the failure to this rule alone. NOT covered by a fixture: the Traslado/@Base rollup sub-case (CFDI40215) and the Retencion/@Importe rollup sub-case (CFDI40211) -- no Retenciones node is present in either fixture at all.
